facts.raw_span: A woman in her 30s presented with a painful bruise on her hand
the bruise and pain had persisted despite icing and resting the area
She denied any personal or family history of bleeding disorders
An ill-defined indurated blue-green plaque was noted on the dorsum of the left hand
Radiography: Showed soft tissue swelling but were otherwise unremarkable
Magnetic Resonance Imaging: Showed a heterogeneously fluid hyperintense and T1 heterogeneously hyperintense lesion measuring approximately 1.6 × 0.5 × 2.9 cm
Mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition
Lesional cells were spindled, ovoid, and epithelioid, with open chromatin, prominent nucleoli, and without mitoses
Mixed inflammatory infiltrate including neutrophils, histiocytes, and foamy macrophages
Immunohistochemistry: Strongly positive for CD34; negative for S100, SOX10, HMB45, and Melan-A
Soft green-blue plaque on the dorsal hand
H&E stain demonstrating spindled cells surrounding fat globules

concepts.why: The presence of a blue-green plaque, mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue, and lesional cells with open chromatin and prominent nucleoli support this diagnosis
The combination of a painful bruise, soft tissue swelling, and a lesion with mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue is consistent with this diagnosis

rationales.F04: Blue-green plaque is consistent with both Nodular pseudolipomatosis and Hemosiderotic fibrolipomatous tumor
rationales.F07: Extensive pigment deposition is more characteristic of Hemosiderotic fibrolipomatous tumor
rationales.F08: Spindled and epithelioid cells are consistent with both Nodular pseudolipomatosis and Hemosiderotic fibrolipomatous tumor
rationales.F10: Strong positivity for CD34 and negativity for S100, SOX10, HMB45, and Melan-A support the diagnosis of Hemosiderotic fibrolipomatous tumor and rule out Pigmented villonodular synovitis
rationales.F12: Spindled cells surrounding fat globules are consistent with both Nodular pseudolipomatosis and Hemosiderotic fibrolipomatous tumor

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of a blue-green plaque, mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition, and lesional cells that are spindled, ovoid, and epithelioid, support the diagnosis of Hemosiderotic fibrolipomatous tumor, which is further confirmed by the strong positivity for CD34 and the absence of staining for S100, SOX10, HMB45, and Melan-A.
